feeds.title: Bald and Beautiful
feeds.description: I'm a female and I have alopecia. This blog started out as a form of self-therapy, as I learned how to embrace being bald. Embracing my baldness was the best decision I ever made. I hope that what I post and re-blog here will inspire and empower you, whether you have alopecia, cancer, or shaved your head as a fashion or social statement.

feeds.title: Bald Runner
feeds.description: I am Jovenal 'Jovie' Narcise. I am an active runner and marathoner/ultrarunner presently staying in the Philippines. This blog is about my running (road and trail) as well as Ultrarunning. It will also feature snippets about food, lifestyle, going outdoors, health, and physical fitness. Some of the posts include travels within the Philippines as well as in other countries.

feeds.title: Bald and Fabulous Blog
feeds.description: I have lived with alopecia since I was 8 years old, it took many years of tears and anger, shame and hiding, depression and anxiety to understand that there are many options available for me. So I decided to spread awareness and support for Alopecia Areata through my Bald and Fabulous blog. I believe that whether someone is bald by an autoimmune disease, illness, or from surgery, or by personal choice, they are still fabulous.

feeds.title: Scalp Co. Blog
feeds.description: The official blog of Scalp Co., Here we share and discuss issues regarding hair health, loss, and treatments like micro-pigmentation. Scalp Co. was founded by John Chandler in 2016 and is one of the premium providers of Scalp Micro Pigmentation in the US. We offer one on one full service doing hair fillers for women, treating male pattern baldness, and are an industry leader in hair transplant scar camouflage treatments.

feeds.title: The Bald Gent
feeds.description: The Bald Gent is the leading blog on Men's Hair Loss. We cover a wide variety of topics from lifestyle, grooming, and fashion. Discover more today. Created by Paul Inman, It's The Bald Gent's mission to bring you all the latest lifestyle, grooming, and fashion ideas.

feeds.title: Bald Girls Do Lunch Blog
feeds.description: A blog devoted to helping women with alopecia cope, gain confidence, and feel a sense of community. Bald Girls Do Lunch is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for women with alopecia. We are reserved for providing highly accurate, realistic, and up-to-date information about alopecia areata.

feeds.title: Lady Alopecia Blog
feeds.description: I may not have much hair but yes I do have lots to say. I am Emma, a copywriter, yoga teacher and fancy dress fanatic. I've had alopecia areata on and off for most of my life so I am here to inform you about the disease and its treatments, support and empower women and men with alopecia. Check out my articles on alopecia with top treatments, nutritional advice and stress-busting tips. My tales will surely inform, amuse and maybe even inspire you.

feeds.title: The Bald Brothers Blog
feeds.description: The Bald Brothers are dedicated to anyone dealing with hair loss. We make epic skincare products for all of our readers. Here we share our greatest balding tips for men losing their hair. With our simple and effective skincare routine, you can control your balding easily. Our biggest bit of advice? Embrace the new look!

feeds.title: Balding Blog
feeds.description: Dr. William Rassman is a world-leading expert in hair loss with over 25 years of experience and over 50,000 satisfied clients. Along with Dr. Jae Pak at New Hair Institute they are dedicated to world-class hair restoration. This site exists to educate about hair loss and hair restoration. Get answers to your questions about balding from real physicians.

feeds.title: Bald is Beautiful on Women Blog
feeds.description: What if a female shaves her head just because it looks really cool without having to justify? So, this blog is dedicated to females who are bald or shave their heads. Bald is Beautiful on Women Blog meant to be educational, informative, and entertaining. Ultimately the goal is to normalize the shaved or bald head of females in our society.
